title: Wrong custom performance monitors type when added later in runtime
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.6.2-stable and likely later.

### System information

Windows 11 - Godot v4.6.2.stable - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NIVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070

### Issue description

When calling `Performance.add_custom_monitor(..., Performance.MONITOR_TYPE_PERCENTAGE) or Performance.add_custom_monitor(..., Performance.MONITOR_TYPE_TIME)` at different points during runtime, the later created monitors will not have the correct monitor type and will instead follow the type pattern of previously created custom monitors.

After investigating the engine, the culprit seems to be in `EditorPerformanceProfiler::update_monitors()`. The method is fed the names of the custom monitors and the custom monitor types as two separate lists where,
1. it will create a hashmap of the names
2. then filter the hashmap to remove what monitors already exists
3. finally, and where the issue likely lies, it will set up an index at 0 and iterate through the hashmap and use the index to grab the type from the methods provided array.

I believe the bug can be resolved by retrieving the type from the hasmap value and subtracting `Performance::MONITOR_MAX`

Like so:
```cpp
Performance::MonitorType type = Performance::MonitorType(p_types[E.value - Performance::MONITOR_MAX]);
```
Instead of:
```cpp
Performance::MonitorType type = Performance::MonitorType(p_types[index]);
```

### Steps to reproduce

The issue should be reproduceable by adding a monitor of type A on ready then adding another monitor some frames later of type B.

```gdscript
func _ready():
    Performance.add_custom_monitor(&"TestA", func(): return 1., [], Performance.MONITOR_TYPE_TIME)
    for i in range(100):
        await get_tree().process_frame
    Performance.add_custom_monitor(&"TestB", func(): return 1., [], Performance.MONITOR_TYPE_PERCENTAGE)
```
